title: ConfirmDialog
wrapsNative: alert(_:isPresented:actions:message:), or confirmationDialog(_:isPresented:titleVisibility:actions:message:), with Button(role: .destructive) and Button(role: .cancel)
summary: Confirmation of a consequential action is the system alert, or the confirmation dialog, with a destructive button and Cancel. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Before an action that deletes or cannot be undone. Use confirmationDialog when the person started the action from a control on screen, and alert when the question interrupts. Say in the message what will change.
whenNotToUse: Do not confirm actions that are easy to undo; offer undo. For a choice between several options see choice-dialog.
api: func alert(_ title: String, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, actions: () -> some View, message: () -> some View) -> some View
func confirmationDialog(_ title: String, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, titleVisibility: Visibility = .automatic, actions: () -> some View, message: () -> some View) -> some View
Button(_ title: String, role: ButtonRole?, action: () -> Void)

states.name: presented
states.description: The alert is centred over a dimmed screen; the confirmation dialog rises from the bottom on iPhone and is a popover on iPad.

states.name: destructive
states.description: A button with the destructive role is drawn in red.

states.name: type to confirm
states.description: An alert may contain a TextField; disable the destructive button until the text matches.

appearance: The system draws both in every theme, following the light or dark appearance. Destructive buttons are the system's red, not the theme's danger colour. Monarch does not colour the buttons.
platformNotes: The web ConfirmDialog stays open while the action runs and shows pending and error states, and has a consequences list, a confirm phrase, an acknowledgement checkbox and a reason field. The system alert closes when a button is tapped, so run the action afterwards and show progress and failure on the screen (a loading MonarchButton, a MonarchBanner). The confirm phrase is a TextField in the alert with the destructive button disabled until it matches. The acknowledgement checkbox and the reason field with validation need a sheet of your own. Android uses a Material AlertDialog.
accessibility: System behaviour: the alert is modal, VoiceOver reads the title and message, and focus returns to the presenting control afterwards.
System behaviour: the escape gesture chooses the button with the cancel role.
The destructive role is also spoken by its title, so name the button after the action ("Delete"), not "OK".
edgeCases: An alert with no buttons gets a system OK button.
Only one alert or dialog is presented at a time; a second one waits or is dropped.
With a hardware keyboard, Return activates the default action. Do not make a destructive button the default.
